requirement:
Extend the existing URL-shortener service to support an optional custom alias
when creating a link. Analyze the change against docs/01-business-requirement.md,
docs/02-requirement-analysis.md, docs/03-engineering-design.md, and the current
codebase.

Keep the existing stack, default generated-code behavior, redirect behavior,
analytics behavior, and API response contract compatible for callers that do
not provide an alias. Identify the required request/schema, service, persistence,
migration, API documentation, and test changes. Surface decisions that need
human input, including alias character rules, length limits, reserved values,
and duplicate-alias behavior. Do not add link expiration or other features.

Return a structured draft with affected requirements and components, assumptions,
open questions, risks, ordered tasks with dependencies, tests, and acceptance
checks. Mark it pending human review; do not imply the feature has been approved
or implemented.
summary: Add optional, validated custom aliases to the existing URL-shortener while preserving generated codes and existing API behavior.
functional_requirements: Keep generated codes working when a caller omits a custom alias.
Accept an optional custom_alias when creating a link and preserve existing redirects and analytics.
quality_requirements: Preserve backward compatibility for existing API clients.
Enforce alias uniqueness safely under concurrent creation requests.
Document and test validation and duplicate-alias behavior.
assumptions: Custom aliases are an accepted brownfield extension; they do not alter the original baseline scope.
No expiration behavior is included in this request.
approved_decisions: Aliases contain 3–16 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens and begin/end with a letter or digit; uppercase is rejected.
Reserve api, health, metrics, docs, redoc, and openapi.json.
A duplicate alias returns HTTP 409 with error code short_code_conflict.
Alias and generated codes share the existing unique short_links.code column; its VARCHAR(16) length is sufficient, so no migration is required.
custom_alias is optional; omitted values continue to generate Base62 codes with the existing response contract.
risks: Aliases share a namespace with generated codes, so a requested alias can conflict with an existing generated code; the unique constraint rejects either collision.
